cases.description: A clean friendly static robot already prepared at the intended game scale and pose.
cases.evaluation_note: The provider must accept the clean control without inventing a repair.
cases.expected_piece_count_evidence: The fixture is one assembled clean robot.
cases.title: Clean no-op control

cases.description: A broken static robot that should match the clean robot's scale, upright pose, grounding, and display-name contract.
cases.evaluation_note: The provider must normalize scale and pose and may perform only deterministic display-name cleanup.
cases.expected_piece_count_evidence: The fixture is one assembled robot despite its invalid transform and names.
cases.title: Broken scale and pose

cases.description: A static robot fixture containing one proven zero-area triangle and unreferenced vertex tuples.
cases.evaluation_note: The provider may remove only the proven degenerate triangle and compact its unreferenced vertex data.
cases.expected_piece_count_evidence: The injected degenerate triangle is a defect in one otherwise complete robot.
cases.title: Proven degenerate geometry

cases.description: A friendly courier and repair robot already at an acceptable scale whose geometry and appearance must be preserved.
cases.evaluation_note: The provider should limit changes to deterministic display names and preserve the asset visually.
cases.expected_piece_count_evidence: Patchling is one semantic robot assembled from intentional modeled details.
cases.title: Patchling preservation

cases.description: A stylized lantern for close-up gameplay use that should be 1.2 meters tall, upright, grounded, and visually preserved.
cases.evaluation_note: The provider must correct the extreme source scale and may propose the use-case triangle budget without unsafe topology edits.
cases.expected_piece_count_evidence: The lantern and its modeled construction details form one semantic prop.
cases.title: Shader Lantern normalization

cases.description: One complete riding crop; the source accidentally contains three spatially separated copies and only the central complete crop should remain.
cases.evaluation_note: The provider must identify the duplicate copies and select exact labeled components without welding or guessing.
cases.expected_piece_count_evidence: The description requests one crop and identifies the separated copies as accidental duplicates.
cases.title: Riding crop component selection

cases.description: A quadrupedal robot dog about the size of a city bus whose body and four disconnected modeled legs are all intentional and must be preserved.
cases.evaluation_note: The provider must preserve all five intentional forms and must not mistake articulated construction for duplicate geometry.
cases.expected_piece_count_evidence: The four legs and body are intentional parts of one quadrupedal robot dog.
cases.title: Robot dog component preservation

cases.description: A decorative pet collar with a shattered-heart charm and buckle for normal gameplay. Its current scale, pose, pivot, and intentional construction parts are user-accepted and must be preserved; only excessive mesh complexity should be repaired.
cases.evaluation_note: The provider should reduce excessive mesh complexity to the normal-gameplay budget while preserving all intentional parts.
cases.expected_piece_count_evidence: The collar, charm, buckle, rings, and studs form one wearable asset and must all remain.
cases.title: Shattered-heart collar simplification
